title: Higher isn't always better
about: Why flying too high makes a crash landing, and the math behind it.

html: The higher something falls, the faster it hits the ground.
It isn't simple doubling. Falling from 4 times as high makes it hit only 2 times as fast. But that's still a lot harder.

steps.q: To clear a 4 m semi truck you need about 5 m of height. Your car flew to 13 m and crashed when it landed. What's the best fix?
options: Use less thrust so it flies lower
steps.explain: You only needed 5 m. Flying lower means hitting the ground slower. Engineers use just enough power, not the most.

steps.q: If you drop something from 4 times as high, it hits the ground about...
steps.explain: Speed grows with the square root of height. √4 = 2.
